journey.title: Opt out of reminders with the keyboard after choosing Text message
journey.goal: Arrowing from Text message to the opt-out answer hides the mobile number field that no longer applies

functionalJourney.title: Switch reminder channel with a pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Choosing Email then Text message shows only the mobile number field

guards.title: Choose Email with the keyboard and enter an address
guards.goal: Selecting Email reveals the email address field and the address is kept

plan.root_cause: The radios module only updates ARIA attributes and conditional visibility on click events, not on change events triggered by keyboard navigation, causing conditional panels to remain visible when a different radio is selected via arrow keys.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a change event listener to the radios module that mirrors the click handler logic, invoking setAttributes on radios with aria-controls to ensure ARIA state and visibility are updated when the radio state changes via keyboard.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can now navigate between radio options using arrow keys and see associated conditional content show/hide correctly, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Both click and change listeners may execute for mouse interactions, causing setAttributes to run twice (idempotent).
Minimal performance overhead from additional event listener.
No impact on non-radio elements as listener is scoped to the module.
verification_requirements: Verify that selecting a radio via arrow keys updates aria-expanded and toggles the correct conditional panel visibility.
Verify that mouse clicks continue to work as before.
Verify that choosing 'Text message' then arrowing to 'I do not want reminders' hides the mobile number field.
Verify that choosing 'Email' shows the email input field.
Ensure no regression in existing form submission or validation behavior.

plan.root_cause: The radios component is initialized on two separate modules for the same radio group (name='reminder'). Keyboard navigation between radios in different modules does not trigger change events in the module containing conditional content, so the conditional panel remains visible when the opt-out radio is selected.
plan.repair_strategy: Combine the two radio modules into a single module in the HTML so that all radios in the group are within the same component instance. Additionally, add a change event listener to the radios component to handle keyboard-driven state changes, ensuring conditional visibility updates when arrow keys change the selected radio.

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can navigate between all reminder options (Email, Text message, I do not want reminders) using arrow keys, and the associated conditional panels (email address, mobile number) show/hide correctly, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Combining modules changes the DOM structure but preserves visual layout due to existing CSS classes.
The change event listener may fire twice for mouse interactions (click and change), but setAttributes is idempotent.
No impact on form submission or validation behavior.
verification_requirements: Verify that selecting a radio via arrow keys updates aria-expanded and toggles the correct conditional panel visibility.
Verify that mouse clicks continue to work as before.
Verify that choosing 'Text message' then arrowing to 'I do not want reminders' hides the mobile number field.
Verify that choosing 'Email' shows the email input field.
Ensure no regression in existing form submission or validation behavior.
